title: 3 Keys to Weather the Autonomous Attack Storm

segments.text: Who remembers the saying, "I feel it in
my bones."
When I was a kid, I remember my
great-grandmother. She uh would, you
know, always be able to predict the
weather and I was like, "What what is
this hocus pocus?" Like, "What what is
actually going on here?" And I remember
being an adult many many years after
this and I tore my Achilles doing some
sprints and during the recovery I
remember oh man every time it's about to
rain every time it's about to snow I
felt it in my Achilles and I was like
this is what my great grandmother felt
she could literally feel it in her bones
and I would say that I feel a storm
coming like I genuinely feel it.
Remember all the stuff that came out
from Anthropic last year about
autonomous attacks, all the stuff that
Jacob Klein was talking about yesterday
and how they've approved and involved
all these different things that we're
starting to see. And of course, there
were different folks in the community.
There are folks uh inside of uh you
know, our community either they said,
"Oh, this is the worst thing ever." or
even this is uh something that isn't
that big of a deal. But this is what I
saw. I saw the tip of the iceberg
because I could see a world in which
there are tens of thousands if not
hundreds of thousands of autonomous
malicious agents looking to
for targets of opportunity trying to
take what we are protecting. This is
something that I feel like is a reality.
I just I spend my time working with
leaders across the globe on what are
their biggest concerns from an AI
perspective. What are their concerns
from a cyber security perspective? And
this is a real threat. But here's the
bigger problem. The bigger problem is
that with all this impending stuff that
I think is going to happen, we still
haven't got a lot of the things in order
that we should have gotten in order. Who
here knows about asset management? Have
we solved asset management? Raise your
hand if you've absolutely solved asset
management. Exactly. What what about
identity? Raise your hand if we have
solved workforce identity or what about
non-human identity? Raise your hand. Oh,
and then we were like, you know, that's
not hard enough. Let's bring agent
identity to the party and we'll just
have a big identity party. All these
things have been really tough to
wrangle, right? Incident response. We've
never even been been able to really dip
into the proactive stuff. So, when I'm
thinking about this this coming storm,
when I'm thinking about how do we get
ourselves in order, there are a couple
things that we can do. One of the things
we can do is really look at what is the
most high lever things that we can do to
protect ourselves, right? I think we
need to go back to the basics because I
would say that we're in this calm before
the storm. During this calm, I feel like
we should really be intentional around
what we're doing around things like
asset management, what we're doing
around uh, you know, identity, right? We
got to get identity figured out for
ourselves as in workforce. We need to
get our identities together from a
non-human identity perspective. And we
really need to start to chip down all of
those foundational things that we've
been talking about for years because
it's going to get to a point where we're
we're already fighting fire to fire. So
what are we going to do when all of a
sudden we have these non-stops non-stop
attacks happening? So we really need to
start to get stuff in order. We need to
start to use AI for our own purposes. We
need to fight fire with fire. I do all
of these sessions. I've probably talked
to a few hundred leaders over the last
few months and I would say about 50% are
AI skeptics and this is what I say each
and every time. I say you can no longer
afford to be a skeptic. I said at worst
case you can be cautiously optimistic
but here's the facts. The facts is that
the adversary is using artificial
intelligence and if you're going to try
to keep up you have to fight fire with
fire. You have to understand how do we
leverage these technologies for our own
purposes. Here's an analogy I give folks
because folks say I don't want to use
AI. I was saying I say hey I want you to
imagine this. I want you to imagine you
are the best mathematician in the entire
world and you want to go work at NASA
and you want to work with rockets. In
the interview you let them know, hey,
I'm the best mathematician in the world
but I don't use a calculator. Are they
going to hire you? Are they going to
hire you because you're the best
mathematician but you don't use a
calculator? Because now there's going to
be a high school kid that is just as
good if not better because they use a
calculator. We need to understand how do
we protect AI in our environment because
the attack surface isn't the same. And
the most important thing is governance.
Governance is the most important thing
when it comes to artificial intelligence
because we have to get everybody in the
organization on the same page. We need
to forget about this whole outsourcing
myth of like, hey, let's replace our
level ones with AI. That's hogwash.
Forget about it. Don't do it for a bunch
of reasons. Number one, if you're
building the future of your organization
and you've replaced all your level ones,
where do your level twos come from in
three years? Where do your level threes
come from in five years? Your leaders,
it doesn't work. The only thing we can
do is pull everybody together and work
together as a team.
One last thing I'll say is I wrote this
for the community and there are a bunch
of folks in this room that have helped
peer review this entire thing and I'm
hopeful that this is going to help folks
when it comes to this coming storm and
we can dance through the raindrops
together. Thank you.
